title: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off
lede: Sierra, the customer experience company co-founded by Bret Taylor, raised $1.75 billion in a Series F at a $30 billion valuation, twice what it was worth under six months ago.

points: Greenoaks and Lightspeed led the round, with Benchmark, Sequoia, GV and Tiger Global among returning investors.
Sierra says it serves almost half of the Fortune 50, with clients including BNY, HSBC, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase and Cox Automotive.
The company said last month that outcome-based pricing helped double run-rate revenue to $400 million in five months.
The money goes to agent tooling for customer service and to more sales staff to close enterprise deals.
Sierra is drafting protocol definitions with Meta, Stripe and Walmart for agents that interact with enterprise systems.

sections.text: Customer service is one of the few areas where enterprises are adopting agents quickly, and Sierra's protocol work is an early attempt at a shared way for outside agents to talk to company systems.
